mainTopic: When to fast for plagues and other dangers, and stories of humility and hidden merit
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: three deaths on one day, or spread over four days, are not a דֶּבֶר. In דרוקרת three people died on one day and רב נחמן בר רב חסדא declared a fast. רב נחמן בר יצחק pointed out that this fits only רבי מאיר's minority view about an ox's gorings. That exchange leads to a warm back-and-forth about who should move to whom, with רבי יוסי's teaching that a person honors his place, proved from הר סיני and the אהל מועד. Two stories follow, about a plague in סורא and a fire in דרוקרת. In each, a neighborhood was protected not by a great rabbi but by an ordinary person's kindness. Next come cases where אמוראים fasted over locusts, a pig plague, a distant plague in בי חוזאי, and a plague in ארץ ישראל. The גמרא explains why each danger could reach them. Finally, the story of אבא אומנא the bloodletter shows how his modesty, his care for the poor and his generosity to scholars earned him daily greetings from Heaven. The story of אביי's test of him continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Deaths on one day or over four days are not a plague
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that three deaths on one day, or spread over four days, do not count as a דֶּבֶר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the three deaths happened on one day or over four days, this is not a plague.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last line of a ברייתא about when a town counts as having a plague. Three deaths only count if they come on three days in a row. One day or four days does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא said that a town sending out 500 soldiers is in a plague if three people die on three days in a row. This line rules out two other patterns. Three deaths on one day could be chance. Three deaths over four days are too spread out to show a pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Plague; a deadly disease spreading through a town

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that three deaths in one day is NOT a plague. The point is that a plague shows itself as a steady pattern day after day, not one bad day.

phrases.english: On one day or over four days
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא: three deaths on three days in a row is a plague.

phrases.english: this is not a plague.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיוֹם אֶחָד אוֹ בְּאַרְבָּעָה יָמִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three deaths on a single day, or spread over four days, do not make a town count as having a דֶּבֶר.

steps.title: The story of דרוקרת and the fast
steps.stepSummary: In דרוקרת, a town that sent out 500 soldiers, three people died on one day, and רב נחמן בר רב חסדא declared a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: דרוקרת was a town that sent out five hundred foot soldiers. Three dead were carried out of it on one day. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא declared a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that seems to go against the ברייתא we just learned. It is setting up the next step, where someone questions this fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דרוקרת is exactly the size the ברייתא describes, 500 soldiers. But the three deaths came on one day, which the ברייתא just said is not a plague. Even so, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא treated it as one and declared a תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: Foot soldier; used to measure the size of a town

phrases.english: Drokart, a city that sent out
five hundred foot soldiers, was

phrases.aramaic: וְיָצְאוּ מִמֶּנָּה שְׁלֹשָׁה מֵתִים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and three dead were carried out of it on one day.

phrases.aramaic: גְּזַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא תַּעֲנִיתָא.
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda declared a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרוֹקֶרֶת, עִיר הַמּוֹצִיאָה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת רַגְלִי הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case of three deaths in one day, the very pattern the ברייתא said is not a plague.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא declared a fast over three deaths on a single day.

steps.title: This fast only fits the view of רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the fast fits only רבי מאיר, who uses a קל וחומר from an ox that gored three times close together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: According to whom did you declare this fast? It must be according to רבי מאיר. He said: if an ox's gorings were spread apart, the owner is liable; if they were close together, is it not all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק questions the fast. He shows that it rests on the reasoning of רבי מאיר, whose view is not the accepted one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox becomes a שׁוֹר מוּעָד (a known dangerous ox) after goring three times. The רבנן require three separate days. רבי מאיר says gorings close together are even more of a warning sign, by a קל וחומר. Treating three deaths in one day as a plague uses the same logic, so the fast follows רבי מאיר and not the majority רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose opinion does this follow?)
All the more so; a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not agreeing with the fast. By saying 'this is like רבי מאיר,' he is quietly pointing out that it follows a minority opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the same idea working in two areas of הלכה. The question is whether events crowded close together count as a pattern. The ruling on the ox tells us how to rule on the plague.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Meir,
who said: if it spread its gorings apart, the owner is liable;
phrases.notes: This is about an ox that gored three times and becomes a שור המועד, whose owner pays full damages.

phrases.english: if it brought its gorings close together, is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the fast in step 2 by tying it to a minority view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fast declared by רב נחמן בר רב חסדא over three deaths in one day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fast only works with רבי מאיר's קל וחומר that close-together events are a stronger sign. The הלכה follows the רבנן, who require separate days, so the fast goes against the ברייתא.

steps.title: An invitation to come and live with us
steps.stepSummary: Impressed, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא invites רב נחמן בר יצחק to come and live in his town.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא said to רב נחמן בר יצחק: Let the master get up and come to us.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of arguing back, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא admires the sharp point and invites רב נחמן בר יצחק to move to his town. This sets up the reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halachic discussion turns into a personal exchange. By inviting him, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא is showing that he accepts the criticism and respects the one who made it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda said to him,
to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak:
Let the master get up and come to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the criticism in step 3 with admiration rather than a defense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An invitation to רב נחמן בר יצחק to come and live with רב נחמן בר רב חסדא.

steps.title: A person honors his place
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק turns down the invitation by quoting רבי יוסי: a place does not honor a person; a person honors his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned in a ברייתא that רבי יוסי says: It is not a person's place that honors him. Rather, a person honors his place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the invitation with a teaching from רבי יוסי. A person's honor does not come from where he lives; the person is what gives the place its worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving to a more important town would not add to his honor. A person can stay where he is and bring honor to that place himself. The next step brings רבי יוסי's proof.

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:
Rabbi Yosei says:
It is not a person's place that honors him;
rather, a person honors his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּנֵינָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the invitation in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב נחמן בר יצחק will move to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's town.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. A person's honor does not depend on his place; the person brings honor to his place.

steps.title: Proof from הר סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves his point from הר סיני. It was off-limits while the שכינה rested on it, and open once the שכינה left.
steps.simpleTranslation: For so we find with הר סיני. As long as the שכינה rested on it, the תורה said: 'Neither let the flocks nor the herds graze facing that mountain.' Once the שכינה left it, the תורה said: 'When the שופר sounds long, they may go up the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a proof from the תורה. הר סיני was holy only because of what was on it, the שכינה, and not because of the mountain itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the שכינה was there, even animals could not graze near the mountain. As soon as the שכינה left, people were allowed to go up. So the holiness came from what rested there, not from the place, just as a person gives honor to his place.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling: three deaths in one day is not a דֶּבֶר, and a fast for it follows only רבי מאיר. The lesson: a person gives honor to his place, just as the שכינה made הר סיני holy.

phrases.english: For so we find with Mount Sinai:
as long as the Divine Presence rested on it,
the Torah said:
"Neither let the flocks nor the herds graze
facing that mountain."
Once the Divine Presence left it,
the Torah said:
"When the shofar sounds long, they may go up the mountain."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּהַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבי יוסי's teaching from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's teaching that a person honors his place, and not the other way around.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two פסוקים about הר סיני (שמות 34:3 and שמות 19:13): the mountain was off-limits only while the שכינה was there.

steps.title: Second proof: the Tent of Meeting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings a second proof from the אהל מועד. While it stood, people with צרעת were sent away. Once it was packed up, זבים and מצורעים could enter that same spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: We find the same thing with the Tent of Meeting in the desert. As long as it was set up, the Torah said to send every מצורע out of the camp. Once its curtains were rolled up, זבים and מצורעים were allowed to go in there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a second proof to back up his point that a place gets its honor only from what is on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ground where the אהל מועד stood was holy only while the אהל was there. Once it was taken down, even people who are normally kept out could walk in. This matches הר סיני and shows again that the holiness belongs to what rests there, not to the land.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the portable משכן in the desert
A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction
People with a bodily discharge that makes them טמא
Curtains (here, the coverings of the אהל מועד)

phrases.english: And similarly we find with the Tent of Meeting that was in the desert,
that as long as it was set up,
the Torah said:
"And they shall send out of the camp every leper,"
once the curtains were rolled up,
phrases.notes: This means the אהל was packed up so the camp could travel on.

phrases.english: זבים and lepers were permitted to enter there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second proof, added to the הר סיני proof
steps.raayaObject: A place does not honor a person; a person honors his place
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rules of the אהל מועד: מצורעים were sent away while it stood and allowed in once it was packed up (במדבר 5:2)
steps.whatToRemember: Holiness and honor come from what rests on a place, not from the place itself. So רב נחמן בר יצחק has no need to move to be honored.

steps.title: Then I will come to you
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא accepts the point and offers to move to רב נחמן בר יצחק instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, let me get up and come to you, master.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב נחמן בר יצחק will not move, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא offers to go to him and learn from him. This sets up the reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with רבי יוסי's teaching. He just turns the invitation around: if the great person should not move, then the lesser one should come to the great one.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case
Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא is speaking to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: If so,
let me get up and come to the master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, נֵיקוּם אֲנָא לְגַבֵּי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the refusal and its proofs with a new offer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא offers to move to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

steps.title: Better the lesser lineage comes to the greater
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק refuses again. Someone of plain family background should go to someone of distinguished family, not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is better that a 'hundred, son of fifty' come to a 'hundred, son of a hundred,' and that a 'hundred, son of a hundred' not come to a 'hundred, son of fifty.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק turns down the second offer too. He uses a money image to say that he should be the one to show honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנה is worth 100 and a פרס is worth 50. Both men are scholars, so each is a 'מנה'. But רב נחמן בר רב חסדא is the son of a great scholar, רב חסדא, while רב נחמן בר יצחק's father was not. So out of humility he says the one with the plainer background should not trouble the one with the finer lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth 100 דינרים; here a picture of a great scholar
Half a מנה (50 דינרים); here a picture of a plainer person

steps.confusionAlert: 'בן פרס' describes the father, not the man himself. Both rabbis are 'מנה'. The difference is only whose father was the greater scholar.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Better that a "hundred, son of fifty" should come
phrases.notes: He means himself: a scholar whose father was an ordinary man.

phrases.english: to a "hundred, son of a hundred,"
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן בר רב חסדא, a scholar who is the son of a scholar.

phrases.english: and a "hundred, son of a hundred" should not come
to a "hundred, son of fifty."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּטָב יָבֹא מָנֶה בֶּן פְּרָס אֵצֶל מָנֶה בֶּן מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and declines the offer made in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scholar from a plainer family should go to the scholar from a distinguished family, so רב נחמן בר רב חסדא should not move.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rabbis try to give honor to the other. רב נחמן בר יצחק's final answer means that he, the 'son of a פרס', should be the one to go to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא, and not the other way around.

steps.title: A plague in סורא spares רב's neighborhood
steps.stepSummary: A plague hits סורא but not the area around רב, and people assume it is because of רב's great merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא there was a plague, but in רב's neighborhood there was no plague. People concluded that it was because of רב's great merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a plague and tells us what the people assumed. This sets up the correction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The natural guess is that the greatest צדיק around is protecting everyone near him. The story states this guess on purpose so that the dream can overturn it.

keyTerms.meaning: They concluded from this, they assumed

phrases.english: In Sura there was a plague,
but in Rav's neighborhood there was no plague.
They concluded from this
that it was because of Rav's merit, which is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא הֲווֹת דְּבַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story connected to the theme of disasters and the merit that protects from them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People assumed רב's merit saved his neighborhood from the plague.

steps.title: The dream: it was the man who lent burial tools
steps.stepSummary: A dream tells the people that rescue from a plague was too small a thing for רב's merit. The real cause was a man who lent out his hoe and shovel for burials.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was shown to them in a dream: רב's merit is very great, and this matter is too small for רב. Rather, it is because of a certain man who lends his hoe and shovel for burials.
steps.whatsHappening: A dream corrects what the people assumed. The protection came from an ordinary man's kindness, not from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream does not lower רב. It says his merit is far too big to be 'used' on something this small. The plain man who helped bury the dead earned this protection through his steady, quiet חסד.

keyTerms.meaning: It was shown to them in a dream
A hoe and a shovel (or basket), used for digging

phrases.english: It was shown to them in a dream:
Rav, whose merit is very great,
this matter is too small for Rav.
Rather, it is because of a certain man
who lends a hoe and a shovel for burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְחֲזִי לְהוּ בְּחֶילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the assumption made in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The people's guess that רב's merit saved the neighborhood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saving people from this plague was too small a matter for רב's great merit; the credit belongs to a man who helped with burials.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that simple, practical kindness can carry enough merit to protect a whole neighborhood.

steps.title: A fire in דרוקרת spares רב הונא's neighborhood
steps.stepSummary: A fire breaks out in דרוקרת but does not reach רב הונא's area, and people credit רב הונא's great merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: In דרוקרת there was a fire, but in רב הונא's neighborhood there was no fire. People concluded that it was because of רב הונא's great merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story built the same way as the first and states the people's assumption. This sets up another dream correction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the people give the credit to the great rabbi nearby. The repeated pattern tells the learner to expect the same kind of twist.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in בבל, the same town from the fast story earlier

phrases.english: In Drokeret there was a fire,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא לָא הֲווֹת דְּלֵיקְתָּא.
phrases.english: but in Rav Huna's neighborhood there was no fire.
They concluded from this
that it was in the merit of Rav Huna, which is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְרוֹקֶרֶת הֲווֹת דְּלֵיקְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story following the same pattern as steps 10 and 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People assumed רב הונא's merit saved his neighborhood from the fire.

steps.title: The dream: it was the woman who shared her oven
steps.stepSummary: A dream reveals that this was too small for רב הונא. The real cause was a woman who heated her oven and let her neighbors use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was shown to them in a dream: This is too small for רב הונא. Rather, it is because of a certain woman who heats her oven and lends it to her neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: The dream corrects the people again. A woman's generosity with her oven, not רב הונא's merit, kept the fire away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kindness fits the rescue: she shared her fire for good use, and the destructive fire stayed away from her neighborhood. Together with the plague story, the lesson is that everyday sharing protects a community.

phrases.english: It was shown to them in a dream:
This is too small for Rav Huna.
Rather, it is because of a certain woman
who heats her oven and lends it to her neighbors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְחֲזִי לְהוּ בְּחֶילְמָא: הַאי זוּטְרָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the assumption made in step 12, the same way step 11 overturned step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The people's guess that רב הונא's merit saved the neighborhood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saving the area from the fire was too small a matter for רב הונא's merit; the credit belongs to a generous neighbor.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories the great rabbi's merit is 'too big' for the rescue. The neighborhood was protected by a regular person's practical חסד.

steps.title: Locusts arrive and רב יהודה declares a fast
steps.stepSummary: People tell רב יהודה that locusts have come, and he declares a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רב יהודה: Locusts have come. He declared a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. Locusts show up, and רב יהודה right away declares a public fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locusts are a classic danger to crops, so a fast is a natural response. This story sets up the next step, where the people question whether it was really needed.

keyTerms.meaning: locusts (a type of grasshopper that eats crops)

phrases.english: They said to Rav Yehuda:
Locusts have come.
He decreed a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה: אֲתוֹ קַמְצֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories of hidden merit to stories of fasts declared because of danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrival of locusts is a reason to declare a fast.

steps.title: The people object that the locusts are not causing damage
steps.stepSummary: The people tell רב יהודה the locusts are not destroying anything, so why fast?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: They are not causing damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The people push back on רב יהודה's fast. They say the locusts are not really harming the crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that a fast is for real harm, and right now there is no harm. This questions whether the danger is serious enough yet.

phrases.english: They said to him: They are not causing damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לָא קָא מַפְסְדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fast declared in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's decision to fast over the locusts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no damage yet, so there is no reason for a fast.

steps.title: רב יהודה answers that the locusts did not bring their own food
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה replies: Did they bring food with them? They will eat your crops soon.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Did they bring provisions with them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the people with a sharp question. The locusts have no other food, so they will surely eat the crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the danger counts even before the damage starts. If the threat is certain to come, you fast now.

phrases.english: He said to them: Have they brought provisions with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זְווֹדֵא אַיְיתוֹ בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the damage, though not yet happening, is certain to come.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No damage now means no reason to fast.
steps.terutzMaskana: A certain coming danger is enough reason to fast now.

steps.title: A plague among pigs and רב יהודה declares a fast
steps.stepSummary: People report a deadly disease among the pigs, and רב יהודה declares a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רב יהודה: There is a plague among the pigs. He declared a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story about רב יהודה. This time the danger is a disease killing pigs, and he declares a fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising because the plague is only hitting animals, not people. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step about why he fasted.

phrases.english: They said to Rav Yehuda:
There is pestilence among the pigs.
He decreed a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה: אִיכָּא מוֹתָנָא בַּחֲזִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about רב יהודה declaring a fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה declared a fast over a plague among pigs.

steps.title: Does רב יהודה hold that a plague in one species spreads to all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב יהודה fasted because he holds a plague in one kind of animal spreads to every kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יהודה holds that a plague sent against one species is sent against all species?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out the reason behind רב יהודה's fast. It suggests a general rule he might hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this were his reason, then any plague in any animal would call for a fast. The גמרא raises this possible rule so it can test it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds, he is of the opinion
a plague that has been sent (a spreading plague)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Yehuda holds
a plague sent against one species
is sent against all species?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא קָסָבַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what principle explains the fast in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יהודה's fast shows he holds that a plague in one species spreads to all species.

steps.title: No, pigs are different because their insides are like humans'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: pigs are special because their intestines resemble those of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, pigs are different, because their intestines are similar to those of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea from the last step. רב יהודה does not need a general rule; pigs are a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because pigs' insides are like humans', a disease in pigs could spread to people. So the fast was about danger to humans, not about every animal plague.

phrases.english: No, pigs are different —
as their intestines are similar to those of people.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, שָׁאנֵי חֲזִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested rule of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב יהודה holds every animal plague spreads to all species.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion missed that pigs are a special case, since their bodies resemble humans'.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say רב יהודה holds the opposite rule. It only says this story does not prove the general rule, because pigs are an exception.

steps.title: A plague in בי חוזאי and שמואל declares a fast
steps.stepSummary: שמואל hears of a plague in the distant region of בי חוזאי and declares a fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to שמואל: There is a plague in בי חוזאי. He declared a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story with שמואל. A plague breaks out in a faraway place, and he still declares a fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising part is the distance. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: בי חוזאי, a region far from שמואל's home in בבל

phrases.english: They said to Shmuel:
There is pestilence in Bei Ḥozai.
He decreed a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל: אִיכָּא מוֹתָנָא בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, now about a plague far away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל declared a fast over a plague in a distant region.

steps.title: The people object that the place is far away
steps.stepSummary: The people tell שמואל: But that place is far from here!
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But it is far away!
steps.whatsHappening: The people challenge שמואל's fast. The plague is far off, so why should they fast?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes a distant plague is no threat to us. This questions whether distance makes the danger irrelevant.

phrases.english: They said to him: But it is far away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: וְהָא מְרַחַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fast declared in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's fast over a faraway plague.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plague that far away is not a danger here, so there is no reason to fast.

steps.title: שמואל answers that nothing in between will stop it
steps.stepSummary: שמואל replies that there is no crossing between here and there that would block the plague.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: There is no crossing here that will stop it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. Nothing separates the two places, so the plague can travel all the way here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Distance alone does not protect people. What matters is whether something blocks the path, and here nothing does.

keyTerms.meaning: a crossing, like a river crossing

phrases.english: He said: There is no crossing here
phrases.notes: He means a river or similar barrier between the places that would block the plague from spreading.

phrases.english: that will stop it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: לֵיכָּא מַעְבָּרָא הָכָא דְּפָסֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the distance is not a real barrier.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A faraway plague cannot reach us.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without a barrier in between, a distant plague can still spread here, so we fast.

steps.title: A plague in ארץ ישראל and רב נחמן fasts in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן hears of a plague in ארץ ישראל and declares a fast, reasoning that if the mistress is struck, surely the maidservant will be.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רב נחמן: There is a plague in ארץ ישראל. He declared a fast, saying: If the lady of the house is struck, surely the maidservant will be!
steps.whatsHappening: A final story. רב נחמן, living in בבל, declares a fast over a plague in ארץ ישראל and explains why with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ארץ ישראל is compared to the lady of the house and בבל to her maidservant. If the more important place is not spared, the less important place certainly will not be.

keyTerms.meaning: the lady of the house, the mistress

phrases.english: They said to Rav Naḥman:
There is pestilence in Eretz Yisrael.
He decreed a fast
saying: If the lady of the house is afflicted,
phrases.notes: The lady is ארץ ישראל; the maidservant is בבל, where רב נחמן lived.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so for the maidservant!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן: אִיכָּא מוֹתָנָא בְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story of fasting over a faraway plague, this time with its own built-in reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plague in ארץ ישראל is a reason to fast in בבל, by קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: In all four stories, the אמוראים fasted even when the danger seemed small, limited to animals, or far away. Each time the reason was that the danger could still reach them: locusts will eat the crops, pig disease can pass to people, nothing blocks a distant plague, and if ארץ ישראל is struck, בבל surely will be.

steps.title: Challenge: why did שמואל fast for a place that is not the 'mistress'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from רב נחמן's reasoning that a plague in one maidservant land should not cause a fast in another. It then challenges this from שמואל, who fasted for a plague in בי חוזאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason רב נחמן fasted is that ארץ ישראל is the mistress and בבל is the maidservant. That implies that for two maidservant places, there is no fast. But שמואל was told of a plague in בי חוזאי, and he declared a fast!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רב נחמן's 'mistress and maidservant' reason and shows that it seems to clash with what שמואל did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reason suggests that only a plague in a more important place (ארץ ישראל) spreads concern to a less important place. But בי חוזאי and נהרדעא are both outside ארץ ישראל, two 'maidservants,' and still שמואל declared a fast. So the 'mistress' reason seems not to be the full story.

keyTerms.meaning: Mistress, lady of the house (here ארץ ישראל)
Maidservant (here the lands outside ארץ ישראל)
But look! (opens a challenge from another source)

phrases.english: The reason is because it is a mistress and a maidservant,
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב נחמן in step 23: ארץ ישראל is the mistress and בבל is the maidservant.

phrases.english: which implies that with a maidservant and a maidservant — no fast.
But they told שמואל:
There is a plague in בי חוזאי,
and he decreed a fast!
phrases.notes: This is the story from steps 20–22. Both places are outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּגְבִירָה וְשִׁפְחָה, הָא שִׁפְחָה וְשִׁפְחָה — לָא. וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב נחמן's reasoning in step 23 and sets it against שמואל's practice in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that only a 'mistress' plague causes a fast in a 'maidservant' land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל fasted when both places were 'maidservants,' so the mistress-maidservant relationship cannot be required.

steps.title: Answer: caravans travel between those places
steps.stepSummary: The case of שמואל is different, because caravans regularly travel from בי חוזאי, and the plague can come along with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Since caravans travel from there, the plague can come along with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that שמואל had a different reason to worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one 'maidservant' land does not need to fear another's plague. But between בי חוזאי and שמואל's town there was regular caravan traffic, so the disease could actually travel with the people. This fits שמואל's own words in step 22 that nothing blocks the way between them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (marks a special case)
Along with it, together with them

phrases.english: It is different there,
since there are caravans
and the plague joins them and comes along with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא שַׁיָּירָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a special factor exists in שמואל's situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's fast shows that any distant plague, even between two 'maidservant' lands, calls for a fast.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two 'maidservant' lands normally do not fast for each other, unless caravans link them and can carry the plague.
steps.whatToRemember: A fast for a faraway plague is declared when ארץ ישראל (the 'mistress') is struck, or when regular travel links the two places.

steps.title: אבא אומנא received greetings from Heaven every day
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: אבא אומנא the bloodletter got greetings from the heavenly yeshiva every day, אביי every Friday, and רבא only every ערב יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא the bloodletter would receive greetings from the ישיבה in Heaven every day. אביי received them every ערב שבת, and רבא every ערב יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about an ordinary worker whose good deeds earned him great honor in Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is the order: a simple bloodletter was greeted more often than the great sages אביי and רבא. This sets up the question of what made him so special.

keyTerms.meaning: A bloodletter (someone who draws blood for health)
The eve of a day (the day before)

phrases.english: Abba the bloodletter
would have greetings come to him
from the yeshiva in Heaven every day,
and to Abaye every Shabbat eve,
and to Rava every Yom Kippur eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא אוּמָּנָא הֲוָה אָתֵי לֵיהּ שְׁלָמָא מִמְּתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about the merits of ordinary people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A simple bloodletter received daily greetings from Heaven, more often than great sages.

steps.title: אביי is upset, and is told he cannot do what אבא does
steps.stepSummary: אביי felt bad that אבא אומנא was honored more than he was. He was told from Heaven that he could not match אבא's deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was upset because of אבא the bloodletter. They said to him: You are not able to do what he does.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is troubled by the difference in honor, and he gets a short answer that points to אבא's special deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say אבא is greater in Torah. It says his daily deeds are something אביי cannot do. This prepares the next step, where the גמרא asks what those deeds were.

phrases.english: Abaye was upset
because of Abba the bloodletter.
They said to him:
phrases.notes: The גמרא does not say who 'they' are. In context the answer seems to come from Heaven.

phrases.english: You are not able to do as his deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁא דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: אביי reacts to the difference in honor described in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא's honor comes from deeds that even אביי could not match.

steps.title: What were אבא אומנא's deeds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what special deeds אבא the bloodletter did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what were the deeds of אבא the bloodletter?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא is preparing to list אבא's good deeds in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said אביי could not do 'his deeds' but did not say what they were. Here the גמרא asks for the details.

phrases.english: And what were the deeds of Abba the bloodletter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי הֲווֹ עוֹבָדֵיהּ דְּאַבָּא אוּמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the deeds mentioned in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific deeds that earned אבא daily greetings from Heaven

steps.title: His care for modesty with patients
steps.stepSummary: אבא treated men and women separately, and he had a special garment for women so he would not see them uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he did bloodletting, he put the men in one place and the women in another. He had a garment with an opening where the cupping horn goes. When a woman came, he dressed her in it so he would not look at her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: אבא was extremely careful about modesty while doing his work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting meant uncovering part of the body, so a bloodletter could easily see people exposed. אבא arranged his work so that this would not happen: separate rooms for men and women, and a special garment for women.

phrases.english: That when he would do the procedure,
phrases.notes: Literally 'the matter.' It means the bloodletting.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַחֵית גַּבְרֵי לְחוֹד וְנָשֵׁי לְחוֹד,
phrases.english: he would place men separately and women separately,
and he had a garment
that had in it a place for the horn
which was slit open where the cut is made.
When a woman came to him,
he would dress her in it,
so that he would not look at her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי הֲוָה עָבֵיד מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He kept strict modesty: men and women apart, and a special garment for women.

steps.title: A hidden box so the poor are not embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: אבא had people put payment in a hidden place, so anyone who could not pay would not be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a hidden place where people put the coins he charged. Whoever had money put it there, and whoever did not have money was not embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of אבא's deeds: he set up payment in a way that protected poor people's dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because no one saw who paid, a poor person could get treatment without being shamed. אבא was willing to lose money so that no one would feel embarrassed.

phrases.english: And he had a hidden place
where people would throw in the coins that he charged,
so whoever had money would throw it in,
and whoever did not have money was not embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִית לֵיהּ דּוּכְתָּא דִּצְנִיעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second deed in answer to step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He protected poor people from shame by having payments put in a hidden place.

steps.title: Free treatment and money for תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אבא took no payment from a young תלמיד חכם, and even gave him money afterward to buy food to heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a young תלמיד חכם came to him, he would not take payment from him. After the scholar got up, אבא would give him coins and say: Go and heal yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists another deed: אבא's special generosity to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did more than treat scholars for free. He also paid them so they could buy healthy food after losing blood. This shows how much he honored people who learn תורה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: When a young Torah scholar happened to come to him,
he would not take payment from him.
And after the scholar got up,
he would give him coins and say to him:
Go, heal yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה אִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third deed in answer to step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He treated Torah scholars for free and gave them money to recover.

steps.title: אביי sends two rabbis to test אבא, and he hosts them warmly
steps.stepSummary: אביי sent two rabbis to check on אבא. אבא seated them, gave them food and drink, and spread out mats for them to sleep on at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day אביי sent a pair of rabbis to test him. He sat them down, fed them, gave them drink, and at night spread out mats for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new part of the story begins: אביי tests how far אבא's goodness goes. This sets up what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only heard about how אבא treated his patients. Now we see him welcome guests with full hospitality. The story of the test continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: To test him, to check on him

phrases.english: One day Abaye sent
a pair of rabbis to test him.
He sat them down, fed them, and gave them drink,
and at night he spread out mats for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁדַּר אַבָּיֵי זוּגָא דְרַבָּנַן לְמִיבְדְּקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אבא אומנא with אביי's test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא showed full hospitality to the rabbis אביי sent to test him.
